captive_summary: The BW Tatiana FSRU at Acajutla regasifies LNG and sends the gas 1.8 km by subsea pipeline to the ONSHORE Energia del Pacifico (EDP) power plant - a well-documented PowerPlantsSupplied relationship, not captive power for the terminal itself. EDP's own 380 MW of generation (19x Wartsila 18V50SG gas engines + 1 steam turbine) belongs to the power plant, not to the FSRU/terminal. No source found this session describes the BW Tatiana vessel's OWN onboard hotel/regasification power plant (fuel or hardware), which is the actual captive-power question for this terminal.
confirmed_how: POWER Magazine, 'Feat of Engineering Provides Floating Power Solution' (quoting Invenergy VP Jose Sarmiento): 'Energia del Pacifico, or EDP...is a 380-MW power plant fueled by natural gas, with the fuel supplied via pipeline from an LNG floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU)'; and caption: 'Permanently moored at El Salvador's Port of Acajutla, the BW Tatiana is the first floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU) on the Pacific Coast of the Americas. [LNG] delivered to the FSRU is converted to natural gas that is transported via a 1.8-kilometer subsea pipeline to the onshore power plant.' Same article: 'The EDP combined cycle power plant features 19 Wartsila 18V50SG natural gas-powered reciprocating engines, each rated at 18.9 MW, and one 28-MW steam turbine generator.' This confirms the direction test (gas flows FROM the terminal TO the plant) but does not address the FSRU's own onboard power generation, which was not found in any source reachable this session (BW Group fleet pages 404; SEC EDGAR has no BW-specific filing; Marginalia/Wayback/general web search all unproductive or blocked for 'BW Tatiana' + generator/engine terms).
